method: Manually inspected close side-by-side canonical/scene crops. Crops preserve aspect ratio and use fit-contain, not geometry warping. No facial similarity model or numeric measurement was used. Head pose, expression and warm scene lighting were considered; accessory presence was not accepted as identity proof.
findings: The prior identity approvals were too permissive. Clothing, hair color and green equipment were being treated as sufficient evidence.
The 20 new Signal Processing phase images inherited drift from retained briefing scene references and further changed faces.
Canonical portraits included after scene reference in the 8 pending Browser images improved some details, but did not reliably lock Demir identity.
Retained baseline briefings already have the same facial drift. Fixing only new phases would leave inconsistency.
Nazari is generally more consistent than Farah and Demir, particularly pending Why the Browser takeaways. Her age lines must remain a separate gate.
correctionStrategy: Use canonical portrait references first, target scene last. Explicitly label identity sources and scene edit target.
Edit only heads, hair and neck transitions; preserve bodies, hand contacts, furniture, diagram values, composition and lighting.
State immutable facial proportions, nose tip and nostril width, cheek volume, chin, brow/eye shape, stubble/age lines and accessory geometry.
Inspect a paired crop for every visible character at every output. Do not approve merely because clothing and accessories match.
Review whole scene again after face edits for unintended body, graph, text or background changes.
Use independently reviewed pilot output as evidence that the prompt works, not as a replacement for each asset gate.

rootPilotReview.farah: Broader nose tip, straighter brows, lower cheek volume, rounded chin and adult eye/mouth lines restored. Corrected face reads as the anchor at a three-quarter angle.
rootPilotReview.demir: Round nose, eye spacing, broad lower face, freckles, uneven stubble and below-lip patch restored. Earpiece and front lock are much closer. Minor elevated hair spike variation is acceptable.
rootPilotReview.wholeScene: Visible bodies, hand contacts and diagram remain coherent. This is visual review, not pixel invariance certification.

checks.accessories: Green AR lens and earrings remain. These identify the role, but do not establish matching facial identity.

faces.specificObservation: Mature features remain close; thinner nose and cheek/jaw shape are moderate differences.

checks.facialProportions: Recognizable mature broad face, but some views narrow the lower cheek and chin more than the anchor.
checks.eyesBrows: Dark firm brows and skeptical eye shape usually remain; several views exaggerate the slant and lashes.
checks.noseJaw: The angular jaw is recognizable; nasal width and rounded tip are sometimes reduced.
checks.skinAge: Tan skin, forehead lines and gray hair remain. In several Signal scenes, crow feet and mouth folds are softened.
checks.hair: Short gray-streaked bob remains recognizable; the gray pattern and puffed crown vary.
checks.accessories: Olive engineering clothing is consistent. It does not compensate for facial differences.

faces.specificObservation: Long pointed nose and hard beard outline plus expanded hair mass remain.

checks.facialProportions: The lower face is longer or more sharply cut than the softly squared canonical jaw.
checks.eyesBrows: Eye openings are often more almond-shaped and smaller relative to face width; brow shape is more sharply angled.
checks.noseJaw: The nose is narrower and more pointed in most three-quarter views; chin is more tapered or projected.
checks.skinAge: Freckles usually remain, but stubble becomes a more uniform outlined beard. Some small faces read younger than the anchor.
checks.hair: Quiff is usually taller and more uniformly spiked than the compact, irregular canonical locks.
checks.accessories: The comms unit remains but changes size and housing; it sometimes occupies the opposite visible ear. That needs a consistent side rule.
